transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net advanced technical operations, my name is Sarah. How can I assist you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hello Sarah. I'm calling about our gigabit full fibre connection. I run continuous network telemetry monitoring from my home server, and over the past forty-eight hours, our optical line has been suffering intermittent packet frame drops. When I checked the internal ONT diagnostic status page, the optical receive power level was reading marginal at negative twenty-eight point two dBm.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can certainly understand your concern when seeing marginal optical power levels near receiver sensitivity thresholds, Jasper. Negative twenty-eight dBm is right on the edge of optical budget, so let's inspect the exchange OLT telemetry together and get that signal stabilized.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you Sarah, I really appreciate speaking with someone who understands optical metrics.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Before we pull the headend telemetry graphs, let's complete account verification. Could you confirm your full name and the installation address?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Jasper Thorne, 15 Millbank Court, Norwich, NR3 1BL.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And what is the security PIN on your account, Jasper?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you Jasper, verification is complete. So what I understand is your full fibre connection is logging intermittent frame drops, and your local ONT receiver telemetry indicates a degraded optical power level of negative twenty-eight point two dBm, which you want stabilized to ensure continuous gigabit throughput, is that right?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, exactly that. Standard GPON sensitivity floor is negative twenty-eight, so any slight optical fluctuation causes bit errors.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: What model of optical network terminal is mounted on your wall?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It's the white Nokia G-010G-Q standalone ONT.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And what are the LED indicator lights showing on the Nokia ONT right now?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Power is green, LAN is flashing green, and PON is solid green, but occasionally the Alarm LED flickers red for a fraction of a second.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Bear with me for a moment while I query the Nokia OLT chassis at the Norwich Central exchange to check the launch power on your GPON port.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for holding, Jasper. I have pulled the port telemetry on card four. The exchange OLT laser launch power is completely normal at plus four point two dBm.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: So the launch power is healthy, which means we have nearly thirty-two dB of optical path loss between the exchange and my ONT.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Exactly. Normal optical distribution network loss should be around twenty to twenty-two dB.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Could there be an unseated connector or dust contamination on the optical patch cord?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That is the single most common cause of a sudden six to eight dB power drop. Obviously optical fiber connectors are extremely sensitive to microscopic dust particles or slight seating misalignment.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: While we are looking at the line, what type of router is plugged into the ONT LAN port?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I have a custom pfSense firewall router running on an Intel quad-core mini PC.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: pfSense handles gigabit PPPoE and NAT routing with very low packet jitter.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, CPU usage never exceeds fifteen percent even under full gigabit loads.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And you don't have any sharp ninety-degree bends in the white optical fibre lead leading to the wall box?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, the fiber follows a gentle curved conduit radius along the baseboard.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That protects the silica glass core from micro-bend optical attenuation.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, I made sure to observe the minimum fifty-millimeter bend radius during installation.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And the wall CSP box has an internal protective splice tray safeguarding the external pigtail.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Good to know the external entry point is weather-sealed.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And your Norfolk exchange area is scheduled for XGS-PON multi-gigabit upgrades next year.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I will definitely be upgrading to the two-gigabit tier when that launches.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I can inspect the optical patch cable right now.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I will take direct ownership of this investigation and stay on the line while we inspect the physical connection.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I'm looking at the green SC-APC connector plugged into the bottom of the Nokia ONT.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Is the green connector seated firmly into the click-lock receptacle?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Looking closely at the collar... Actually, the green shroud is sitting about two millimeters proud of the locking clip! It looks like someone nudged the cable when vacuuming!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Gently push the green connector straight into the ONT port until you hear and feel a positive mechanical click.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Pushing firmly... Click! It just clicked right in! The green shroud is completely flush with the socket now!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Excellent. Now look at the Alarm LED on the ONT.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The Alarm LED has gone completely dark! Solid dark, zero red flickering!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Now let me query the OLT real-time optical power polling monitor. Bear with me for thirty seconds.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for waiting, Jasper. The real-time optical receive power level has jumped from negative twenty-eight point two dBm up to negative nineteen point four dBm!

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Negative nineteen point four dBm! That is an eight point eight dB improvement! That's right in the prime center of the optical budget!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Just confirming before we run a stress test, that's on the Nokia G-010G-Q unit, correct?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, the Nokia G-010G-Q.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Now run a five-minute bidirectional throughput and packet loss test from your server.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Starting iperf3 stress test across all eight streams... Download: nine hundred and thirty-eight megabits! Upload: one hundred and ten megabits! Zero dropped frames across one hundred thousand packets!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That confirms zero optical packet loss and rock-solid optical headroom.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That was such an elegant, clean resolution Sarah. You saved us waiting for an engineer visit for what was just a loose click-lock connector.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Just to confirm your billing contact email on file, it's jasper dot thorne at eastanglia dot co dot uk, correct?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, that's my primary email.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I will log the optical telemetry improvement from minus twenty-eight to minus nineteen dBm in your permanent service history.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you Sarah, you've been brilliant.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Is there anything else regarding your gigabit line that I can assist with today, Jasper?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No Sarah, the line is performing at peak efficiency. Thank you so much.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It was my absolute pleasure. Thank you for choosing S-Net, Jasper, and have a wonderful day.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you Sarah, goodbye.
